newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Iscor gives go-ahead to minerals project.
newsitem.headline: Iscor gives go-ahead to minerals project.

text.p: South African steel and mining giant Iscor Ltd said on Monday its board had given approval to a 1.65 billion rand heavy minerals project.

The mining division will now proceed with detailed design for the project which will comprise a mine in Northern province near Gravelotte, a mine in KwaZulu-Natal near Richards Bay and a central processing complex including a smelter near Richards Bay.
The project will be capable of producing an annual 220,000 tonnes of titania slag, 130,000 tonnes of pig iron, 15,000 tonnes of rutile and 35,000 tonnes of zircon.
The go-ahead for the scheme follows the strategic acquisition of a controlling stake in Australia's Ticor Ltd in 1995 to gain entry into the heavy minerals industry.
"This is a demonstartion of Iscor's commitment to diversify its minerals and mining business," said mining managing director Ben Alberts.
Products from the project wil be exported via Richards Bay and are expected to generate over 750 million rand in foreign exchange from 2000.
The combined reserves of the mining locations are sufficient for a mining life of 20 years.

When in full production, the scheme is expected to boost South Africa's titanium production by some 20 percent, ensuring the country remains the largest producer of titania slag in the world, followed by Canada and Norway.
